created_trees.objective: Demander un candidat mesuré combinant le noyau à bases de lignes et directive SIMD OpenMP de T2 avec la parallélisation OpenMP persistante et le partitionnement par lignes de T1. Partir du candidat T2 le plus rapide; éviter le parallélisme imbriqué, conserver les barrières entre pas, respecter threads et toutes les contraintes de correction. Comparer aux deux sources aux budgets d’un et quatre cœurs; ne pas présumer que les gains s’additionnent.
created_trees.stop_condition: Ne retenir la combinaison que si elle passe les contrôles et améliore les mesures comparables; sinon conserver le meilleur parent correct pour l’assemblage.
created_trees.subject: Combiner SIMD sur x et parallélisme OpenMP par lignes

created_trees.objective: Partir du noyau fusionné correct de Gm1 et tester la réutilisation des voisins contigus sur x (par exemple par déroulage et réemploi de valeurs en registres) afin de réduire les chargements redondants du stencil de rayon 3. Conserver les bénéfices mesurés du parcours par lignes et de l’équipe OpenMP persistante, sans modifier le compilateur ni supposer un alignement ou une taille fixes. Vérifier la tolérance et mesurer à un et quatre cœurs, tous coûts inclus.
created_trees.stop_condition: Écarter toute variante incorrecte; arrêter après deux essais mesurés sans amélioration reproductible face au parent, et conserver alors le candidat Gm1.
created_trees.subject: Réduire les chargements redondants en x dans le noyau fusionné

created_trees.objective: Combiner le candidat T2 d96 (bases de lignes, sans directive SIMD, avec restrict pour l’aliasing) au parallélisme persistant par lignes de T1, en partant de d96. Évaluer la combinaison à un et quatre cœurs contre Gm1 et ses parents, sans présumer que leurs gains s’additionnent; préserver la correction et les contraintes du protocole.
created_trees.stop_condition: Ne retenir cette combinaison que si elle est validée et améliore le score officiel de Gm1; sinon conserver Gm1 comme meilleur candidat mesuré.
created_trees.subject: Combiner l’auto-vectorisation avec le parallélisme persistant

decision.rationale: Examiner le programme mesuré Gm1 avant de choisir une intégration assembly; ses transformations sont connues au résumé, mais le code complet ne l’est pas.
Comparer l’ordonnancement réel de Gm2 à celui de Gm1 avant de choisir une intégration ciblée; leurs temps mesurés sont proches, mais le code diffère.

Use measured, correct Gm1 as the base (0.054595 s, score 0.894909). Test whether Gm2’s persistent, contiguous z-slab ownership improves on Gm1’s static collapsed worksharing while retaining Gm1’s hoisted row pointers and guarded OpenMP SIMD x-loop. Preserve the six-step recurrence, buffer parity, full initialization, thread budget, and synchronization between dependent steps. Gm2 is also correct but slightly slower overall (0.055090 s), so this is an unverified interaction to measure, not an assumed gain. Do not carry over T4’s x-unrolling variants, which were slower than Gm1.

Inspect the correct, measured T2 candidate 2023bb before choosing another integration. Its reported 0.079497 s is the best standalone T2 result, and its aliasing annotations may complement the current SIMD stencil and persistent slab schedule. The code details are needed to adapt only a relevant transformation.

children.objective: Replace the serial sweeps with OpenMP work over disjoint rows or slabs, honoring the threads argument as a CPU budget. Compare a team created for each timestep with a persistent team spanning all six steps, measuring any fork/join savings against synchronization and buffer-parity handling. Ensure workers finish each timestep before the next reads its output. Preserve full initialization, update bounds, and boundaries. Test correctness and native wall time at one and four cores, including initialization and overhead.
children.subject: Compare per-step and persistent OpenMP teams

children.objective: Optimize the contiguous-x radius-3 update, contrasting a compiler-vectorizable loop with explicit SIMD only when supported by the frozen target configuration. Do not change compiler settings or assume row alignment; handle tails and generic n. Preserve the recurrence, full initialization, and boundaries, and validate the fixed tolerance. Measure both core budgets and include any setup costs.
children.subject: Contrast compiler auto-vectorization and target-supported SIMD

children.objective: Focus on temporal reuse across the six dependent steps. Compare a spatial-only tiled control with a halo-aware multi-step tile, holding the spatial kernel and threading strategy fixed within the comparison to isolate temporal reuse. Respect radius-three dependencies, produce both full output buffers with baseline initialization and boundaries, and include scratch allocation in timing. Avoid benchmark-size specialization; validate correctness and measure one- and four-core wall time.
children.subject: Isolate temporal blocking from spatial-only cache blocking

Do not carry over T4’s x-unrolling variants, which were slower than Gm1.

children.objective: Replace the serial sweeps with OpenMP work over disjoint rows or slabs, honoring the threads argument as a CPU budget. Compare a team created for each timestep with a persistent team spanning all six steps, measuring any fork/join savings against synchronization and buffer-parity handling. Ensure workers finish each timestep before the next reads its output. Preserve full initialization, update bounds, and boundaries. Test correctness and native wall time at one and four cores, including initialization and overhead.
children.subject: Compare per-step and persistent OpenMP teams

children.objective: Optimize the contiguous-x radius-3 update, contrasting a compiler-vectorizable loop with explicit SIMD only when supported by the frozen target configuration. Do not change compiler settings or assume row alignment; handle tails and generic n. Preserve the recurrence, full initialization, and boundaries, and validate the fixed tolerance. Measure both core budgets and include any setup costs.
children.subject: Contrast compiler auto-vectorization and target-supported SIMD

children.objective: Focus on temporal reuse across the six dependent steps. Compare a spatial-only tiled control with a halo-aware multi-step tile, holding the spatial kernel and threading strategy fixed within the comparison to isolate temporal reuse. Respect radius-three dependencies, produce both full output buffers with baseline initialization and boundaries, and include scratch allocation in timing. Avoid benchmark-size specialization; validate correctness and measure one- and four-core wall time.
children.subject: Isolate temporal blocking from spatial-only cache blocking
